newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities deflated after ECI.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities deflated after ECI.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were lower in late afternoon trading as bond prices rallied early on benign fourth quarter employment cost index, dealers said.

"They (volatilities) came in very high this morning in anticipation of the employment cost index, and after that they were just sold down," said a trader with a brokerage firm at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for CBOT March T-bond futures options stood at around 10.6 percent in late afternoon business, down from Monday's closing of 11.3 percent.

The U.S. Labor Department announced early in the session that fourth-quarter ECI was up 0.8 percent, a touch below the average Wall Street forecast of 0.9 percent. The index had risen 0.6 percent in the third quarter.
March T-bond futures jumped by more than a full point soon after the data to touch a session high of 111-2/32 before surrendering about half of that gain by late trade.
Traders said the ECI was not necessarily weak but probably was not strong enough to prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten credit at the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting on February 4-5.

Order flows in the options pit were heavy. Among the largest trades, an investment bank was said to have bought 5,000 contracts of March 108-110 put spread. Another bank was seen trading 5,000 legs of a "combo" involving a sale of 110 puts and purchase of 112-114 call spreads.

Despite the deflated levels today, traders said volatilities for fixed-income options were likely to stay well suppported for a while as the market awaits several pieces of economic data in coming weeks and the FOMC meeting. Fourth-quarter gross domestic production is due out on Friday.

"I think, from the other numbers that are coming in this week, perception is that the locals have been trying to hold it (implied volatility) up a little bit," a Eurodollar trader for a bank affiliate at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options stood at 12.3 and 14.8 percent, off about a quarter point from Monday.
